Video Illustrator

Your voice, your assets, any look you choose.

简体中文

An Agent Skill that turns your own narration and your real material (book cover, course cover, screenshots, logo, kept exactly as they are) into a 20–60 second promo or concept explainer in the style you pick. You get an MP4 and editable scene source, rendered on your own machine.

One narration, six looks

The same 20.86-second narration (the author's own voice) and the same real book cover in every cell. Previews are silent loops; click one for the full video with narration and music.

Each preview links to the full video (with narration and music) on YouTube; the two v0.4 cells also link to Bilibili, the four v0.5 cells to an MP4 you can play directly. This repository does not distribute the MP4 files themselves. Every sample was made from a one-sentence request with Claude Code + Opus 5.5 (high effort) in the author's environment, each in a single pass with 0 revisions: two with Skill 0.4, four with Skill 0.5. Skill 0.4 fixes a concept and one organizing device before any keyframe, puts a new picture on every bar, snaps text to the voice and checks a contact sheet before delivery (the cinematic request also carried a director's note). Skill 0.5 adds motion parameters with a restraint budget, a vocabulary of transitions and the craft of each medium; before delivery an independent reviewer with a clean context checks the film against the aesthetic rules, and the three rules that decide whether a stranger stops (would a stranger stop, pictures and scale, leave the desk) can get a second round. The four 0.5 samples reuse the music of the earlier sample in the same style (generated with Lyria); no new Lyria call was made. The exact requests, Skill versions, time, cost at API list price and music sources are in SAMPLES.md, which also keeps the records of the earlier versions of these four styles. A small style page plays each sample and copies a ready-made request for that style.

One mechanism, three looks

The same 15-second explainer insert (silent, no narration) in the three styles that carry a mechanism best: the structure of the second-generation Tesla Roadster, from the car to its contact patches, suction fans, air tanks and cold-gas thrusters and back. One content file, three renders; every figure on screen comes from a research table and is attributed. Details in SAMPLES.md; all three stacked in one clip.

How it works

  1. Put your material in folders (all optional):

    my-promo/
  inputs/voice/    your narration (a recording or a cloned-voice export); optional .srt or words.json with word times
  inputs/assets/   book or course covers, screenshots, logos: used as-is, only scaled, moved, cropped or lit
  inputs/brand/    brand pack: brand.json (display_name, palette, fonts...) + optional fonts, motifs, end card

  2. Ask in one sentence, naming a style:

    Use video-illustrator on ./my-promo: my narration is in inputs/voice, my book cover in inputs/assets, brand info in inputs/brand. Make a 1920×1080 promo in cut-paper style with subtitles, timed to the narration. Don't invent anything the material doesn't say.

  3. Get the film and its source: an MP4, the editable scene.html, a brief.md recording the choices (music, beat grid, what happens when) and the assets it used, so you can revise and re-render.

Without any folders the Skill works from text alone, for example "explain why a cache makes repeated requests faster as a 20-second whiteboard animation". A standalone author credit uses display_name from brand.json; words printed on your assets are never changed. Colors follow the chosen style, with your assets' colors as an accent, unless your brand pack colours the whole film. node scripts/brand.mjs --sheet inputs/brand --out brand-sheet.png renders one page to approve the pack before any film is made. To have your own taste in every project, keep a default pack in ~/.config/video-illustrator/brand/ (or point $VIDEO_ILLUSTRATOR_BRAND at one); its rules_docs can list your own design-rule documents, which are read where they are before every film.

For cinematic or trailer requests the Skill takes a 3D route (three.js on your GPU: real lighting, depth of field, motion blur, your cover on a 3D book). Illustration styles stay 2D.

Explainer mode (new in 0.7) is for narration you already have. Give it your video's subtitles and a time window, and it cuts that passage (scripts/excerpt.mjs), shows what the narration describes as a few persistent parts with things moving between them, each change landing on the sentence that says it, and returns silent 16:9 and 9:16 inserts for your own edit plus narrated, captioned previews. See explainer.md.

Episode mode (new in 0.9) makes a whole narrated science or tech explainer of two to ten minutes: an angle, research into a fact table where every number on screen is cited, an explanation plan, a segmented script, official footage, one 3D or 2D scene that carries the mechanism, alignment of your narration take, and a captioned master, rendered segment by segment so a change re-renders only that segment. Bring the narration yourself: your own recording, or an export from the voice service you use; the Skill aligns to it and does not synthesise a voice. The Roadster episode was made this way. See episode.md.

Since 0.9 every mode picks its look from the same style atlas: explainers and whole episodes default to a bright 3D diagram look (diagram-3d), and can instead use any atlas style that can carry a mechanism, on the 3D route or on a 2D starter that reads the same content (for example particles or cut paper). The atlas says which styles fit and why the others do not (styles.md).

Install

Designed for Claude Code + Opus 5.5. Other hosts are unverified.

Requirements:

  • Node.js 20 or newer
  • FFmpeg and ffprobe on your PATH
  • Playwright Chromium (installed below)
  • Optional, for generated music: your own OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment. Music comes from Google Lyria 3 through OpenRouter, a paid call of about US$0.04 per 30-second clip, made only when you authorize it. Sound effects are synthesized locally for free. You can also point the Skill at music you already have. Keyframes or asset images can be sent as reference images with the music request (up to 10) so the score follows the picture; the Gemini API (GEMINI_API_KEY) is supported as an alternative provider.

Keep the video-illustrator folder intact and place it in your skill directory (for Claude Code, project-local .claude/skills/video-illustrator/, or a symlink to your checkout). Then, from the skill folder:

npm ci
npx playwright install chromium

npm ci also installs the pinned three.js (MIT) used by the 3D route. Rendering runs locally; nothing is sent to a hosted rendering service. Your coding agent still needs its own model access.

GPU rendering (3D route): verified on macOS with an Apple M4 Pro, where --gpu uses ANGLE on Metal; a 1080p frame of the starter scene took about 0.3 s with film grain. Without a GPU, Chromium falls back to software rendering, which works but measured 2× to 15× slower depending on motion blur. GPU rendering on Windows, Linux and other GPUs has not been tested.

Scope

Early preview, best-effort maintenance. This is code-driven animation, not a photorealistic video model or an automatic fact checker, and one sentence will not always give a finished film. Longer narratives, fonts and audio can need extra work. Watch the result and check its claims before publishing. Reproducible issues and focused PRs are welcome.

More

  • Style atlas: all style directions and how to choose. Most have no sample yet.
  • SAMPLES.md: how each showcase film was made.
  • VALIDATION.md: what has actually been tested.
  • Credits: research acknowledgments and third-party licenses.
  • Rendering: renderer contract, drafts, audio-first workflow.
  • Explainer mode: turn one passage of an existing narrated video into a mechanism insert.
  • Episode mode: a whole narrated explainer, from research to a captioned master.
